Bug_Details:
Use of "YYYY" (week year) in a date pattern without "ww" (week in year). You probably meant to use "yyyy" (year) instead. “YYYY” in a date pattern means “week year”. The week year is defined to begin at
the beginning of the week that contains the year’s first Thursday. For example,
the week year 2015 began on Monday, December 29, 2014, since January 1, 2015,
was on a Thursday. “Week year” is intended to be used for week dates, e.g. “2015-W01-1”, but is
often mistakenly used for calendar dates, e.g. 2014-12-29, in which case the
year may be incorrect during the last week of the year. If you are formatting
anything other than a week date, you should use the year specifier “yyyy”
instead.
Bug_Explanation: The code uses 'YYYY' in the date pattern which refers to the week year instead of the calendar year. This can lead to incorrect date formatting, especially at the end or beginning of the year. The intended use here is likely 'yyyy' for the calendar year.
Trigger_Explanation: The bug is triggered because the SimpleDateFormat in showBug is using 'YYYY' for the year, representing the week year instead of the calendar year. This causes incorrect formatting for dates that fall in the last or first days of a calendar year.
Bug_Trigger_Explanation: The test run results indicate that both tests passed without any failures, confirming that the bug was not triggered. If the bug was present, the tests would have failed due to incorrect date formatting.
